identity.title: Gene Therapy for Inherited Platelet Disorders: From Proof of Concept to Clinical Translation.

content.abstract: Inherited platelet disorders (IPDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of rare genetic diseases affecting platelet production and/or function, with clinical manifestations ranging from mild mucocutaneous bleeding to severe hemorrhage, multisystem disease, and predisposition to hematologic malignancy. Treatment remains predominantly supportive, and curative options are limited. Future translation will require disease-specific selection of gene addition, allele-specific approaches, or precise genome editing, together with safer conditioning, efficient lineage-restricted correction, and rigorous long-term assessment of genotoxicity and clonal evolution. A shared hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells platform combined with disease-specific genetic engineering may ultimately enable curative treatment of selected severe IPDs.
